sentences.en: But if they saw you with somebody else or they saw you at a rally, you'd get another card.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们看到你和别人在一起，或者看到你参加集会，你就会再得到一张卡片。

sentences.en: And sort of through that process, they kept track of connections.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，他们追踪了各种人际关系。

sentences.en: And when you got three of these index cards, then they would actually formally open a Carpeta on you.
sentences.zh: 当你集齐三张这样的索引卡时，他们就会正式为你建立一份“档案”。

sentences.en: At the time, it was generally known within the independence movement that the government was watching.
sentences.zh: 当时，独立运动内部普遍知道政府在监视他们。

sentences.en: But how close and in what ways remained a mystery?
sentences.zh: 但监视有多严密、以何种方式进行，依然是个谜。

sentences.en: The police, of course, didn't have the manpower to surveil each and every person who sympathized with the cause.
sentences.zh: 当然，警察没有足够的人力去监视每一个同情该事业的人。

sentences.en: And so they paid friends, neighbors and colleagues to do a lot of the dirty work.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们花钱雇佣朋友、邻居和同事来做很多肮脏的工作。

sentences.en: This, of course, created an obvious incentive.
sentences.zh: 这当然创造了一种显而易见的动机。

sentences.en: If you had something to say, you get paid.
sentences.zh: 如果你有话要说，就能拿到钱。

sentences.en: Or if you were in trouble with the law for whatever reason, you could get out of trouble by helping the police.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你因为某种原因惹上了官司，可以通过帮助警察来摆脱麻烦。

sentences.en: And at a time when work was hard to come by on the island, lots of people suddenly had lots to say.
sentences.zh: 在岛上工作难找的时候，很多人突然间变得“话很多”。

sentences.en: From my perspective, having read a lot of them and talking to people who were surveilled and scholars and other researchers,
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，在阅读了大量档案并与被监视者、学者及其他研究人员交谈后，

sentences.en: you know, a lot of the information is like made up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多信息都是编造的。

sentences.en: Christopher says that despite the bad information, the Carpetas still served a purpose for the Puerto Rican government.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗说，尽管信息质量很差，但这些“档案”对波多黎各政府仍然有用。

sentences.en: It had the effect of making people in the independence movement feel watched, which made organizing harder.
sentences.zh: 它让独立运动中的人感到被监视，从而增加了组织活动的难度。

sentences.en: The Carpetas were an off-the-book means of suppression, while the state created on-the-book ways to criminalize their activity.
sentences.zh: “档案”是一种非正式的镇压手段，而国家同时也创造了正式的法律途径来将他们的活动定罪。

sentences.en: And the size of the Carpeta indicated how aggressively a person was being surveilled.
sentences.zh: 档案的厚度显示了一个人被监视的激烈程度。

sentences.en: A person with a small Carpeta might never see a cop,
sentences.zh: 档案较薄的人可能永远见不到警察，

sentences.en: while a person with a three-foot-tall Carpeta might have police stationed outside their home and business day after day.
sentences.zh: 而档案有三英尺厚的人，可能每天都有警察驻守在他们的家和公司门外。

sentences.en: The heavier the Carpeta, the heavier it weighed on a person's life.
sentences.zh: 档案越重，对一个人生活造成的压力就越大。

sentences.en: In 1948, the Puerto Rican government passed a law that made it a crime to write, meet, or speak about independence.
sentences.zh: 1948年，波多黎各政府通过了一项法律，将撰写、集会或谈论独立定为犯罪。

sentences.en: had entered the McCarthy era, and this fear of communism trickled down into its relationship with Puerto Rico as well.
sentences.zh: 进入了麦卡锡时代，这种对共产主义的恐惧也渗透到了它与波多黎各的关系中。

sentences.en: There was a fear of any kind of radical person, including Puerto Rican nationalists.
sentences.zh: 人们对任何激进分子都感到恐惧，包括波多黎各民族主义者。

sentences.en: Soon, anyone sympathetic to the cause or even questioning the government would find themselves blacklisted.
sentences.zh: 很快，任何同情该事业甚至质疑政府的人都会发现自己被列入了黑名单。

sentences.en: The police officer would show up to where you worked, and they would talk to your boss and be like,
sentences.zh: 警察会出现在你工作的地方，找你的老板谈话，说：

sentences.en: yeah, you know, we're investigating this person because they're, you know, a little subversive,
sentences.zh: “是的，你知道，我们正在调查这个人，因为他们，你知道，有点颠覆性，
或者我们正在对他们进行刑事调查。”

sentences.en: And more often than not, most people would actually get fired from their jobs.
sentences.zh: 而大多数情况下，这些人最终都会被解雇。

sentences.en: Frustration in the independence movement was growing, especially when the island was granted a new status,
sentences.zh: 独立运动中的挫败感日益增长，尤其是当该岛被授予一种新地位时，

sentences.en: one that provided the illusion of independence.
sentences.zh: 一种提供了独立假象的地位。

sentences.en: decided it was time for things to change with Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 认为波多黎各的情况是时候做出改变了。

sentences.en: Countries around the world were decolonizing their territories,
sentences.zh: 世界各地的国家都在对其领土进行去殖民化，

sentences.en: and suddenly having a colony was not a good look anymore.
sentences.zh: 突然间，拥有殖民地不再是一件光彩的事了。

sentences.en: allowed Puerto Ricans to elect their own governor and ratify their very own constitution and bill of rights.
sentences.zh: 允许波多黎各人选举自己的总督，并批准他们自己的宪法和权利法案。

sentences.en: And with all these big changes, Puerto Rico suddenly had the look, even the smell, of a sovereign country.
sentences.zh: 随着所有这些重大变化，波多黎各突然有了主权国家的样子，甚至气味。

sentences.en: And with these changes came a new name, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 随着这些变化，出现了一个新名称：波多黎各自由邦。

sentences.en: Puerto Rico becomes a commonwealth, and this debate begins.
sentences.zh: 波多黎各成为了自由邦，于是这场辩论开始了。

sentences.en: We now have a constitution, we have self-government.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有了宪法，有了自治政府。

sentences.en: For some Puerto Ricans, the answer to whether or not the island had decolonized was an emphatic yes.
sentences.zh: 对于一些波多黎各人来说，关于该岛是否已经去殖民化的答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: In their eyes, the island had achieved what people had been clamoring for all along,
sentences.zh: 在他们眼中，该岛实现了人们一直呼吁的目标，

sentences.en: more autonomy, and an ability to elect their own leaders, all while still maintaining a relationship with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 更多的自治权，以及选举自己领导人的能力，同时仍与美国保持关系。

sentences.en: In other words, all the benefits of being an American while still being able to call yourself Puerto Rican.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，既能享受作为美国人的所有好处，又能称自己为波多黎各人。

sentences.en: Commonwealth supporters described their status as the best of both worlds because we had guaranteed citizenship
sentences.zh: 自由邦的支持者将他们的地位描述为两全其美，因为我们拥有保障性的公民身份

sentences.en: and guaranteed union with the United States, but also a lot of autonomy, you know, kind of like an independent country,
sentences.zh: 以及与美国的保障性联盟，但同时也拥有很多自治权，你知道，有点像一个独立国家，

sentences.en: but also kind of like a state.
But in my opinion and the opinion of its opponents, it was really the worst of both worlds
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，以及在反对者看来，这实际上是两者的最坏结合，

sentences.en: because you are subject to the power of Congress and you're pretending you're decolonized.
sentences.zh: 因为你受制于国会的权力，却假装自己已经去殖民化了。

sentences.en: To Cristina and many others, the term Commonwealth wasn't a real change in political status.
sentences.zh: 对于克里斯蒂娜和许多其他人来说，自由邦这个词并不是政治地位的真正改变。

sentences.en: Sure, Puerto Ricans had moral autonomy, but they didn't have total autonomy.
sentences.zh: 当然，波多黎各人拥有道德上的自治，但他们没有完全的自治。

sentences.en: Puerto Rico is subject to the control of Congress and Congress can run the show
sentences.zh: 波多黎各受制于国会的控制，国会可以掌控一切，

sentences.en: and it can only have a constitution if Congress lets it.
sentences.zh: 而且只有在国会允许的情况下，它才能拥有宪法。

sentences.en: And if Congress wants to take power away, it can.
sentences.zh: 如果国会想收回权力，它随时可以。

sentences.en: In other words, the term Commonwealth was merely a cover,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，自由邦这个词仅仅是一个掩护，

sentences.en: a word that helped Americans shed their belief that they had a colony,
sentences.zh: 一个帮助美国人摆脱他们拥有殖民地这一认知的词汇，

sentences.en: while at the same time introducing even more uncertainty into the day-to-day lives of Puerto Ricans.
sentences.zh: 同时却给波多黎各人的日常生活带来了更多的不确定性。

sentences.en: This is really how the United States has divided and conquered us.
sentences.zh: 这确实是美国如何分而治之我们的方式。

sentences.en: It basically gaslit us into not knowing what Puerto Rico's status is.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是在对我们进行煤气灯效应式的操纵，让我们不知道波多黎各的地位到底是什么。

sentences.en: We ourselves can't define Commonwealth, or at least we can't agree on a definition.
sentences.zh: 我们自己无法定义自由邦，或者至少我们无法就定义达成一致。

sentences.en: And so we just argue ourselves to death.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只能争论到死。

sentences.en: And the United States doesn't have to do anything.
They can just keep having a colony.
sentences.zh: 他们可以继续维持一个殖民地。

sentences.en: For some in the independence movement,
sentences.zh: 对于独立运动中的一些人来说，

sentences.zh: 这种持续的挫败感演变成了可怕的暴力行为。

sentences.en: In March of 1954, four Puerto Rican nationalists entered Congress and opened fire.
sentences.zh: 1954年3月，四名波多黎各民族主义者进入国会并开火。

sentences.en: No one was killed, but five people were injured.
sentences.zh: 没有人死亡，但有五人受伤。

sentences.en: The shooting ended up intensifying government surveillance on the independence movement.
sentences.zh: 这次枪击事件最终加剧了政府对独立运动的监视。

sentences.en: It also deepened ideological divisions over Puerto Rico's status.
sentences.zh: 它也加深了关于波多黎各地位的意识形态分歧。

sentences.en: After the 1950s, the political alliances on the island generally fell into one of three camps.

sentences.en: We belong to, but we're not part of.
